questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (genus) with List-II (common name) and choose the correct option.
List-I
(a) Aptenodytes
(b) Neophron
(c) Pteropus
(d) Balaenoptera
List-II
(i) Flying fox
(ii) Blue whale
(iii) Penguin
(iv) Vulture
questions.explanation: Aptenodytes is the penguin and Neophron is the vulture; both are birds. Pteropus is the flying fox and Balaenoptera is the blue whale; both are mammals. A common trap is assuming Pteropus is a bird because it flies.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Digestion in cnidarians is both extracellular and intracellular.
Reason (R): Cnidarians exhibit cellular level of organisation, like sponges.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Cnidarians do digest food both extracellularly (in the gastro-vascular cavity) and intracellularly, so A is true. They show tissue level of organisation, not the cellular level seen in sponges, so R is false.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Sponges consist of loose aggregates of cells with only some division of labour among them. Which level of organisation do they show?
questions.explanation: In sponges the cells are not organised into tissues. They form loose cell aggregates, which is the cellular level of organisation. Tissue level begins only with coelenterates.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In coelenterates, the cnidoblasts (cnidocytes) found on the tentacles and body are mainly used for:
options: Locomotion through rows of beating cilia
Anchorage, defence and capture of prey
Secretion of the calcium carbonate skeleton in all members
questions.explanation: Cnidoblasts contain stinging capsules called nematocysts. They are used for anchorage, defence and catching prey, and the phylum name Cnidaria comes from them. Locomotion by ciliated comb plates is a feature of ctenophores, not cnidarians.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements is incorrect?
options: In cockroaches and prawns excretion of waste material occurs through malpighian tubules.
In ctenophores, locomotion is mediated by comb plates.
In Fasciola, flame cells help in excretion
Earthworms are hermaphrodites and yet cross fertilization take place among them.
questions.explanation: Cockroaches excrete through Malpighian tubules. Prawns, however, excrete through green glands (antennal glands), so the statement is wrong.
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 4 (MCQ Q8)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Both echinoderms and hemichordates are triploblastic, coelomate animals with an organ-system level of organisation and a complete digestive system.
Statement II: Like chordates, hemichordates possess a closed circulatory system.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.explanation: Statement I matches NCERT for both phyla. Statement II is wrong because hemichordates have an open circulatory system, whereas chordates have a closed one.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The stinging capsules called nematocysts are found inside which cells of coelenterates?
questions.explanation: Nematocysts are contained in cnidoblasts (cnidocytes), which give the phylum the name Cnidaria. Choanocytes belong to sponges, and flame cells belong to flatworms.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In birds, the skin is dry. Which is the only gland present in it?
options: Oil gland at the base of the tail
Sebaceous gland at the base of each feather
questions.explanation: Bird skin has no glands except the oil gland at the base of the tail. Sweat and sebaceous glands are associated with mammalian skin, not avian skin.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
A. Bombyx
B. Laccifer
C. Limulus
D. Locusta
List-II
I. Living fossil
II. Gregarious pest
III. Silkworm
IV. Lac insect
questions.explanation: Bombyx is the silkworm and Laccifer is the lac insect. Limulus (king crab) is a living fossil, and Locusta is a gregarious pest.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following animals have an open type of circulatory system?
Locusta, Balanoglossus, Pheretima, Branchiostoma, Petromyzon, Limulus, Ascaris
questions.explanation: Locusta and Limulus (arthropods) and Balanoglossus (hemichordate) have open circulation, which makes three. Pheretima and the chordates Branchiostoma and Petromyzon have closed circulation, and Ascaris has no circulatory system at all.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: All reptiles have a three-chambered heart, as all amphibians do
Hyla and Salamandra show internal fertilisation and direct development
Chelone and Testudo have dry cornified skin and cannot regulate their body temperature
Ichthyophis, being limbless, is placed in class Reptilia along with snakes
questions.explanation: Turtles and tortoises are reptiles, so they have dry cornified skin and are poikilothermous. Crocodiles have a four-chambered heart, amphibians like Hyla and Salamandra show external fertilisation and indirect development, and Ichthyophis is an amphibian.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Mesoglea is present in between ectoderm and endoderm in Obelia.
questions.explanation: Fasciola (liver fluke) is a platyhelminth, so it is acoelomate, not pseudocoelomate. The other statements are true.
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 4 (MCQ Q7)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (excretory/osmoregulatory structure) with List-II (phylum).
List-I
(A) Flame cells
(B) Malpighian tubules
(C) Proboscis gland
(D) Nephridia
List-II
(i) Hemichordata
(ii) Annelida
(iii) Platyhelminthes
(iv) Arthropoda
questions.explanation: The pairings are: flame cells in flatworms, Malpighian tubules in arthropods, the proboscis gland in hemichordates and nephridia in annelids.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following cartilaginous fishes possesses electric organs?
questions.explanation: Torpedo has electric organs. Trygon (sting ray) is the trap: it has a poison sting, not electric organs. Pristis is the saw fish and Scoliodon is the dog fish.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which pair consists of two triploblastic, bilaterally symmetrical animals in which the first is acoelomate and the second is pseudocoelomate?
questions.explanation: Taenia is a flatworm and therefore acoelomate, while Wuchereria is a roundworm with a pseudocoelom. Fasciola and Planaria are both acoelomate, Ascaris and Ancylostoma are both pseudocoelomate, and Pheretima is a true coelomate.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which feature is shared by Pheretima and Locusta but is absent in Ascaris?
options: A true body cavity lined by mesoderm
questions.explanation: Annelids and arthropods are both coelomates, whereas Ascaris is a pseudocoelomate. Closed circulation occurs only in Pheretima and malpighian tubules occur only in Locusta. Ascaris also has a complete gut, so that feature does not distinguish it.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (structure in sponges) with List-II (role):
List-I
A. Ostia
B. Osculum
C. Spongocoel
D. Spicules
List-II
I. Central cavity receiving water
II. Support of the body
III. Minute pores for water entry
IV. Opening through which water exits
questions.explanation: The ostia are the entry pores, and the spongocoel is the central cavity. The osculum is the exit, and spicules (or spongin fibres) form the supporting skeleton.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Fertilisation in frogs is external.
Reason (R): Amphibians are oviparous and their development is direct.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Amphibians have external fertilisation and are oviparous, so A is true. Their development is indirect (it passes through a larval stage), so R is false. Direct development is a feature of reptiles.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A marine colonial cnidarian shows a sessile, cylindrical stage that gives rise to umbrella-shaped, free-swimming individuals. These free-swimming individuals in turn give rise to the sessile stage again. Identify the free-swimming form and the mode by which it produces the sessile stage.
questions.explanation: The umbrella-shaped, free-swimming form is the medusa. In metagenesis (as in Obelia), polyps produce medusae asexually and medusae form polyps sexually. Reversing these two modes is the common trap.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (genus) with List-II (common name).
List-I:
A. Physalia
B. Pennatula
C. Gorgonia
D. Meandrina
List-II:
I. Sea-fan
II. Brain coral
III. Portuguese man-of-war
IV. Sea-pen
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: The correct pairs are Physalia = Portuguese man-of-war, Pennatula = sea-pen, Gorgonia = sea-fan and Meandrina = brain coral. The usual trap is mixing up sea-pen (Pennatula) and sea-fan (Gorgonia).
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about ctenophores is incorrect?
options: They bear eight external rows of ciliated comb plates for locomotion
Sexes are separate and fertilisation is internal
They reproduce only by sexual means
questions.explanation: In ctenophores sexes are not separate, and fertilisation is external with indirect development. The other three statements are correct NCERT features.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which of the following chordates does the notochord extend from the head to the tail region and persist throughout life?
questions.explanation: In Cephalochordata, such as Branchiostoma (Amphioxus), the notochord runs from head to tail and is retained for life. Ascidia, Salpa and Doliolum are urochordates, in which the notochord is present only in the larval tail.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The file-like rasping organ in the mouth of molluscs, used for feeding, is called the:
questions.explanation: The radula is the rasping, file-like feeding organ in the mollusc mouth. The mantle is the soft skin fold over the visceral hump, the osculum is the water outlet of sponges, and the proboscis is the anterior body region of hemichordates.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following genera is correctly matched with its common name?
questions.explanation: Ancylostoma is the hookworm. Wuchereria is the filaria worm, Fasciola is the liver fluke and Taenia is the tapeworm, so the other three pairings are swapped.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Development in sponges is described as indirect.
Reason (R): Sponges pass through a larval stage that is morphologically distinct from the adult.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Indirect development means passing through a larval stage that looks different from the adult. This is exactly what sponges show, so R correctly explains A.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which group of animals is mostly asymmetrical, meaning that no plane passing through the centre divides the body into equal halves?
questions.explanation: Sponges (Porifera) are mostly asymmetrical. Coelenterates and ctenophores are radially symmetrical, and flatworms are bilaterally symmetrical.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (genus) with List-II (common name):
List-I: (a) Pinctada (b) Antedon (c) Gorgonia (d) Myxine
List-II: (i) Sea-fan (ii) Hagfish (iii) Pearl oyster (iv) Sea lily
questions.explanation: Pinctada is the pearl oyster (Mollusca) and Antedon is the sea lily (Echinodermata). Gorgonia is the sea-fan (Cnidaria) and Myxine is the hagfish (Cyclostomata). Antedon's name 'sea lily' can wrongly suggest a plant-like cnidarian.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Based on the broad classification of Kingdom Animalia, which one of the following generalisations is correct?
options: Every radially symmetrical animal is diploblastic
Every triploblastic animal possesses a true coelom
Every chordate retains its notochord throughout life
Every animal with organ-system level of organisation is triploblastic
questions.explanation: All phyla from Aschelminthes onwards show organ-system organisation, and all of them are triploblastic. Option 1 fails because adult echinoderms are radially symmetrical yet triploblastic. Option 2 fails for flatworms and roundworms, and option 3 fails because the notochord is replaced in vertebrates and is only larval in urochordates.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In Pheretima, the body is divided externally and internally into segments with serial repetition of at least some organs.
Statement II: The neural system of annelids consists of paired ganglia connected by lateral nerves to a single dorsal hollow nerve cord.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement I correctly describes metamerism in the earthworm. Statement II is wrong because annelids have a double ventral nerve cord; a dorsal hollow nerve cord is a chordate feature.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (body organisation feature) with List-II (example animal).
List-I
A. Body cavity lined by mesoderm
B. Mesoderm present as scattered pouches between ectoderm and endoderm
C. Body cavity absent
D. Undifferentiated mesoglea between ectoderm and endoderm
List-II
I. Ascaris
II. Taenia
III. Pheretima
IV. Adamsia
Choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation: Pheretima (an annelid) is a true coelomate. Ascaris (an aschelminth) is a pseudocoelomate, and Taenia (a flatworm) is an acoelomate. Adamsia is a diploblastic coelenterate with mesoglea between its two layers.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In amphibians, the alimentary canal, urinary tract and reproductive tract open into a common chamber that opens to the exterior. This chamber is called:
questions.explanation: The cloaca is the common chamber into which the alimentary, urinary and reproductive tracts of amphibians open. The other options are cavities found in molluscs, aschelminthes and sponges.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In Urochordata, the notochord is present only in the larval tail.
Statement II: In Cephalochordata, the notochord is replaced by a cartilaginous vertebral column in the adult.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: In cephalochordates such as Branchiostoma, the notochord runs from head to tail and persists throughout life. Replacement of the notochord by a vertebral column happens only in vertebrates.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) Bony fishes have four pairs of gills, each side covered by an operculum.
(ii) Labeo and Catla have skin covered with placoid scales.
(iii) In male Scoliodon, the pelvic fins bear claspers.
(iv) Cyclostomes are freshwater animals that migrate to the sea for spawning.
(v) Teeth of cartilaginous fishes are modified placoid scales that are backwardly directed.
(vi) Osteichthyes mostly show internal fertilisation and viviparity.
questions.explanation: Statements (i), (iii) and (v) are correct. Labeo and Catla are bony fishes with cycloid/ctenoid scales, not placoid scales. Cyclostomes are marine and migrate to fresh water to spawn, and bony fishes usually show external fertilisation and are mostly oviparous.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: In Platyhelminthes, the digestive system is called incomplete because a single opening to the outside serves as both mouth and anus.
Statement II: In arthropods, blood is circulated through a series of vessels of varying diameters (arteries, veins and capillaries), so their circulatory system is of the closed type.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Flatworms have one opening that acts as both mouth and anus, so their digestive system is incomplete. Arthropods have an open circulatory system, in which pumped blood directly bathes the cells and tissues. A closed system with arteries, veins and capillaries is found in annelids and chordates, not arthropods.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are true for phylum Echinodermata?
(a) All members are marine.
(b) An excretory system is absent.
(c) Adults are bilaterally symmetrical while larvae are radially symmetrical.
(d) Fertilisation is usually external.
(e) The mouth is on the dorsal side and the anus on the ventral side.
(f) Sexes are separate.
(g) Development is indirect with a free-swimming larva.
questions.explanation: Statements (a), (b), (d), (f) and (g) are true, which makes five. Statement (c) is reversed, since adults are radial and larvae are bilateral. Statement (e) is also reversed, since the mouth is ventral and the anus is dorsal.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which cartilaginous fish possesses electric organs?
questions.explanation: Torpedo has electric organs. Trygon (sting ray) has a poison sting instead, which is the common mix-up. Pristis is the saw fish and Carcharodon is the great white shark.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following sets of animals share a four chambered heart?
questions.explanation: Most reptiles have a three-chambered heart, but crocodiles have four chambers. Birds and mammals also have four-chambered hearts. Amphibians have three chambers.
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 4 (MCQ Q3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Limulus, the king crab, is often called a 'living fossil'. To which phylum does it belong?
questions.explanation: NCERT lists Limulus (king crab) among the arthropods as a living fossil. Despite its common name, it is not a true crab, and it is not a mollusc or echinoderm.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match the excretory or osmoregulatory structure in List-I with the phylum in List-II.
List-I
A. Flame cells
B. Nephridia
C. Malpighian tubules
D. Proboscis gland
List-II
I. Hemichordata
II. Arthropoda
III. Platyhelminthes
IV. Annelida
questions.explanation: The pairings are flame cells with flatworms, nephridia with annelids, malpighian tubules with arthropods, and the proboscis gland with hemichordates. A common trap is assigning nephridia to flatworms.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A worm-like marine animal has a cylindrical body made of a proboscis, a collar and a trunk. It has a rudimentary notochord-like structure in the collar region, an open circulatory system and a proboscis gland. Which statement about this animal is correct?
options: It belongs to a subphylum of Chordata because it possesses a stomochord
It is a triploblastic coelomate non-chordate with external fertilisation and indirect development
It is a pseudocoelomate with a closed circulatory system like vertebrates
Its stomochord is a true notochord that is replaced by a vertebral column in the adult
questions.explanation: The animal is a hemichordate such as Balanoglossus. It is a triploblastic coelomate now placed as a separate non-chordate phylum, with external fertilisation and indirect development. The trap is the stomochord, which only resembles a notochord and was the old reason for grouping hemichordates under Chordata.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Sponges are described as mostly asymmetrical animals.
Reason (R): In sponges, any plane passing through the centre of the body divides it into two equal halves.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Sponges are mostly asymmetrical, so A is true. Asymmetry means that no plane through the centre gives equal halves. R describes the opposite situation, so it is false.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(a) Teeth of Chondrichthyes are modified placoid scales directed backwards.
(b) Osteichthyes have four pairs of gills covered by an operculum on each side.
(c) Reptiles possess external ear openings in addition to a tympanum.
(d) The skin of birds is dry and lacks glands except the oil gland at the base of the tail.
(e) The heart of crocodiles is three-chambered like that of other reptiles.
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements (a), (b) and (d) agree with NCERT. Reptiles lack external ear openings, with the tympanum representing the ear, and crocodiles are the exception among reptiles in having a four-chambered heart.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The heart of an amphibian such as Rana consists of:
questions.explanation: Amphibians have a three-chambered heart with two auricles and one ventricle. One auricle and one ventricle is the two-chambered heart of fishes.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (genus) with List-II (common name).
List-I: (A) Struthio (B) Aptenodytes (C) Neophron (D) Columba
List-II: (I) Vulture (II) Pigeon (III) Ostrich (IV) Penguin
questions.explanation: Struthio is the ostrich, Aptenodytes the penguin, Neophron the vulture and Columba the pigeon. Struthio and Aptenodytes are easy to swap because both are flightless.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Some parasitic flatworms, such as Taenia, absorb nutrients from the host directly through their body surface.
Statement II: In Aschelminthes, development is always indirect, so the young never resemble the adult.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation: NCERT notes that some flatworms absorb nutrients through the body surface. In roundworms, however, development may be direct (young resemble the adult) or indirect, so Statement II is wrong.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) Ctenophores reproduce both sexually and asexually.
(ii) In Obelia, medusae give rise to polyps by sexual reproduction.
(iii) Digestion in cnidarians is both extracellular and intracellular.
(iv) Fertilisation in ctenophores is internal.
(v) Corals have a skeleton composed of calcium carbonate.
(vi) Ctenophores bear eight external rows of ciliated comb plates that help in locomotion.
questions.explanation: Statements (ii), (iii), (v) and (vi) are correct, so the answer is four. Statement (i) is wrong because ctenophores reproduce only sexually. Statement (iv) is wrong because their fertilisation is external and development is indirect.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: In Chondrichthyes, the notochord persists throughout life.
The mouth is ventral in cartilaginous fishes but mostly terminal in bony fishes.
Cyclostomes have a cartilaginous cranium but a bony vertebral column.
Bony fishes have four pairs of gills covered by an operculum on each side.
questions.explanation: In cyclostomes, both the cranium and the vertebral column are cartilaginous. The other three statements match NCERT's descriptions of cartilaginous and bony fishes.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Sponges show a cellular level of organisation, with cells arranged as loose aggregates.
Statement II: Digestion in sponges is extracellular and takes place in the spongocoel.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation: Sponges are primitive multicellular animals with a cellular level of organisation. Their digestion is intracellular, not extracellular, so Statement II is false.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In cartilaginous fishes such as Scoliodon, the teeth are:
options: absent, since the mouth is suctorial
questions.explanation: The teeth of Chondrichthyes are modified placoid scales and point backward. Cycloid scales occur in bony fishes. A suctorial, jawless mouth is a cyclostome feature.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The water vascular system of echinoderms performs all of the following functions EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The water vascular system helps in locomotion, food capture and transport, and respiration. Echinoderms have no excretory system at all, so excretion is not one of its functions.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: How many pairs of gill slits for respiration are present on the elongated body of a cyclostome?
questions.explanation: Cyclostomes have 6-15 pairs of gill slits. Four pairs of gills covered by an operculum is a feature of bony fishes (Osteichthyes), not cyclostomes.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In flatworms such as Planaria and Fasciola, specialised cells called flame cells are mainly concerned with:
options: Absorption of nutrients from the host
questions.explanation: Flame cells are the osmoregulatory and excretory cells of Platyhelminthes. Nutrient absorption happens through the body surface in some parasitic forms, attachment uses hooks and suckers, and regeneration is a separate property of Planaria.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following annelids is monoecious, meaning a single individual produces both eggs and sperms?
questions.explanation: Earthworms (Pheretima) and leeches are monoecious. Nereis is a dioecious annelid. Ascaris and Asterias are not annelids, and both have separate sexes.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following bony fishes is marine?
questions.explanation: Exocoetus (flying fish) is a marine bony fish. Labeo (Rohu), Catla (Katla) and Clarias (Magur) are freshwater fishes.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) Radial symmetry, diploblastic
(B) Bilateral symmetry, acoelomate
(C) Bilateral symmetry, pseudocoelomate
(D) Bilateral symmetry, metamerically segmented coelomate
List-II
(I) Wuchereria
(II) Hirudinaria
(III) Pleurobrachia
(IV) Taenia
questions.explanation: Pleurobrachia is a radial, diploblastic ctenophore. Taenia is an acoelomate flatworm, Wuchereria is a pseudocoelomate roundworm, and Hirudinaria is a segmented annelid with a true coelom.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The digestive tract of birds has two additional chambers. These are:
questions.explanation: NCERT names the crop and gizzard as the additional chambers in the avian digestive tract. Rumen and reticulum belong to ruminant mammals, and air sacs are respiratory structures.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which of the following animals is an undifferentiated layer, the mesoglea, present between the ectoderm and the endoderm?
questions.explanation: Hydra is a coelenterate. Coelenterates are diploblastic, with mesoglea between the ectoderm and endoderm. The other three animals are triploblastic and have a true mesoderm instead of mesoglea.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In cnidarians, the single opening of the central gastro-vascular cavity, the mouth, is located on the:
questions.explanation: Cnidarians have a gastro-vascular cavity with a single opening, the mouth, borne on the hypostome. The osculum is the water outlet of sponges, while proboscis and collar are body regions of hemichordates.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Given below are types of cells present in some animals. Which of the following cells can differentiate to perform different functions?
questions.explanation: Interstitial cells of cnidarians are undifferentiated cells. They can develop into other cell types such as cnidoblasts and gametes. Choanocytes, gastrodermal cells and nematocytes are already specialised.
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 4 (MCQ Q2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which arthropod is cited in NCERT as a 'living fossil'?
questions.explanation: Limulus, the king crab, is the living fossil among arthropods. Locusta is a gregarious pest, while Laccifer and Bombyx are economically important insects.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following animals are coelomates?
Ascaris, Pheretima, Pila, Taenia, Asterias, Balanoglossus, Wuchereria
questions.explanation: Pheretima (annelid), Pila (mollusc), Asterias (echinoderm) and Balanoglossus (hemichordate) are coelomates. Ascaris and Wuchereria are pseudocoelomates, and Taenia is an acoelomate, so the count is 4.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Cyclostomes are marine but migrate to fresh water for spawning.
Statement II: After spawning, adult cyclostomes migrate back to the ocean.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation: Adult cyclostomes die within a few days after spawning in fresh water. It is their larvae that return to the ocean after metamorphosis, so Statement II is incorrect.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following animals belong to class Reptilia?
Chelone, Bufo, Testudo, Salamandra, Vipera, Hyla, Hemidactylus, Ichthyophis
questions.explanation: Chelone (turtle), Testudo (tortoise), Vipera (viper) and Hemidactylus (wall lizard) are reptiles, which makes four. Bufo, Salamandra, Hyla and Ichthyophis are amphibians; the limbless Ichthyophis and the lizard-like salamander are the usual traps.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding levels of organisation is incorrect?
options: Ctenophores exhibit the tissue level of organisation
Roundworms (Aschelminthes) exhibit the organ-system level of organisation
In flatworms, tissues are grouped to form organs specialised for particular functions
Cells of sponges show no division of labour at all
questions.explanation: NCERT states that some division of labour does occur among the cells of sponges, even though the cells form only loose aggregates. The other three statements agree with the text.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following features are common to BOTH Chondrichthyes and Osteichthyes?
Two-chambered heart; operculum covering the gills; air bladder; poikilothermy; separate sexes; placoid scales; streamlined body; usually external fertilisation
questions.explanation: Both classes share a two-chambered heart, poikilothermy, separate sexes and a streamlined body, giving 4. An operculum, an air bladder and usually external fertilisation belong only to bony fishes, while placoid scales belong only to cartilaginous fishes.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following features is present in Osteichthyes but absent in Chondrichthyes?
questions.explanation: Bony fishes have their gills covered by an operculum on each side. Cartilaginous fishes have separate gill slits with no operculum. The other three features are shared by both classes.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following echinoderms is correctly matched with its common name?
questions.explanation: Antedon is the sea lily. Cucumaria is the sea cucumber, Ophiura is the brittle star, Echinus is the sea urchin and Asterias is the star fish.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following phyla consists of animals in which males and females are distinct individuals (dioecious)?
questions.explanation: Roundworms (Aschelminthes) have separate sexes, and females are often longer than males. Sponges, ctenophores and flatworms are hermaphrodite.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following features are shared by both Taenia (tapeworm) and Ascaris (roundworm)?
(i) Bilateral symmetry
(ii) Triploblastic body organisation
(iii) Internal fertilisation
(iv) Complete alimentary canal
(v) Separate sexes (dioecious condition)
(vi) Excretion through flame cells
(vii) Presence of a body cavity
questions.explanation: Both genera are bilaterally symmetrical and triploblastic, and both show internal fertilisation, giving three shared features. Only Ascaris has a complete gut, separate sexes and a pseudocoelom. Flame cells occur only in flatworms, which are hermaphrodite and acoelomate.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
A. Pristis
B. Betta
C. Myxine
D. Pterophyllum
List-II
(i) Angel fish
(ii) Hagfish
(iii) Saw fish
(iv) Fighting fish
questions.explanation: The correct pairs are Pristis–saw fish, Betta–fighting fish, Myxine–hagfish and Pterophyllum–angel fish. Betta and Pterophyllum are both aquarium fishes, so they are easily swapped.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the mode of fertilisation and type of development?
options: Osteichthyes: fertilisation usually external, development indirect
questions.explanation: NCERT states that sponges have internal fertilisation and indirect development with a distinct larval stage. Ctenophores and echinoderms both show external fertilisation with indirect development. Bony fishes have usually external fertilisation but direct development.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The division Agnatha of subphylum Vertebrata is represented by the class:
questions.explanation: Agnatha (jawless vertebrates) contains only the class Cyclostomata, for example Petromyzon and Myxine. The other three classes have jaws and belong to Gnathostomata.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which of the following groups are cells that perform the same function first arranged into tissues, giving a tissue level of organisation?
questions.explanation: Coelenterates show tissue level of organisation, with similar cells grouped into tissues. Sponges have only loose cell aggregates (cellular level). Platyhelminthes reach the organ level, and annelids the organ-system level.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Both cnidarians and ctenophores show extracellular as well as intracellular digestion
Ctenophores reproduce only sexually, with external fertilisation and indirect development
In Obelia, medusae produce polyps asexually and polyps produce medusae sexually
Sponges are hermaphrodite with internal fertilisation and a larval stage distinct from the adult
questions.explanation: In metagenesis it is the polyps that produce medusae asexually, while medusae form polyps sexually. Option 3 reverses this. The other statements agree with NCERT.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The skin of birds is dry and lacks glands, with one exception. Which gland is present in the skin of birds?
options: Sweat gland on the hind limbs
Oil gland at the base of the tail
Mammary gland on the ventral side
Mucous gland all over the body
questions.explanation: NCERT states that bird skin is dry and has no glands except the oil gland at the base of the tail. Mammary glands are a mammalian feature, and moist glandular skin is typical of amphibians.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Pheretima (earthworm) and Hirudinaria (leech) are monoecious annelids.
Reason (R): Nereis, an aquatic annelid, has separate male and female individuals.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Earthworms and leeches are monoecious, while Nereis is dioecious, so both statements are true. However, the sex condition of Nereis does not explain why earthworms and leeches are monoecious.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which of the following groups can the body be divided into identical left and right halves in only one plane?
questions.explanation: A body that can be divided into identical halves through only one plane shows bilateral symmetry, as in annelids and arthropods. Coelenterates and ctenophores are radially symmetrical, and sponges are mostly asymmetrical.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Reptiles usually have a three-chambered heart. Which of the following reptiles is an exception with a four-chambered heart?
questions.explanation: NCERT notes that the reptilian heart is usually three-chambered but four-chambered in crocodiles. Turtles, lizards and snakes keep the three-chambered pattern.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In some animals the body cavity is not lined by mesoderm; instead, the mesoderm lies as scattered pouches between the ectoderm and endoderm. Which animal shows this type of body cavity?
questions.explanation: This describes a pseudocoelom, which is found in aschelminthes such as Ascaris. Fasciola is acoelomate, while Nereis and Balanoglossus are coelomates.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Locomotion in Pleurobrachia is brought about by:
options: Eight external rows of ciliated comb plates
questions.explanation: Pleurobrachia is a ctenophore (comb jelly). Its body bears eight external rows of ciliated comb plates that help in locomotion. Parapodia belong to Nereis, and the water vascular system belongs to echinoderms.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The notochord, which separates chordates from non-chordates, is best described as a rod-like structure that is:
options: Ectodermally derived and formed on the dorsal side during embryonic development
Mesodermally derived and formed on the dorsal side during embryonic development
Mesodermally derived and formed on the ventral side during embryonic development
Endodermally derived and formed on the ventral side of the gut
questions.explanation: NCERT defines the notochord as a mesodermally derived rod formed on the dorsal side of the embryo. The common trap is to call it ectodermal. That would confuse it with the dorsal nerve cord, which is a separate structure.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
A small, exclusively marine animal has the following features:
- a dorsal hollow nerve cord
- paired pharyngeal gill slits
- a notochord that extends from head to tail and persists throughout life
- no vertebral column at any stage
The animal is most likely:
questions.explanation: A notochord that runs from head to tail and persists for life, with no vertebral column, marks a cephalochordate such as Branchiostoma (Amphioxus). Ascidia has a notochord only in its larval tail. Petromyzon is a vertebrate with a cartilaginous vertebral column. Balanoglossus has only a stomochord.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following features are common to both Aves and Mammalia?
Four-chambered heart; homoiothermy; internal fertilisation; direct development; respiration by lungs; external pinnae; feathers; oil gland at the base of the tail
questions.explanation: Both classes have a four-chambered heart and are homoiothermous. Both also show internal fertilisation, direct development and respiration by lungs, giving five shared features. Pinnae are found only in mammals, while feathers and the tail oil gland are found only in birds.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following sets of animals belong to a single taxonomic group?
questions.explanation: Monkey, chimpanzee and man all belong to the mammalian order Primates. The other sets mix animals from different phyla or classes.
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 4 (MCQ Q6)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are true for members of Phylum Porifera?
(i) They are generally marine.
(ii) They are mostly asymmetrical.
(iii) Digestion is extracellular.
(iv) Sexes are separate.
(v) They reproduce asexually by fragmentation.
(vi) Fertilisation is external.
questions.explanation: Statements (i), (ii) and (v) are true. Digestion in sponges is intracellular, they are hermaphrodite rather than having separate sexes, and their fertilisation is internal.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about Class Amphibia and Class Reptilia are correct?
(i) In both classes, the ear is represented by a tympanum.
(ii) Fertilisation is external in both classes.
(iii) Crocodilus has a four-chambered heart, whereas Rana has a three-chambered heart.
(iv) Both classes are oviparous with indirect development.
(v) Ichthyophis is a limbless reptile.
questions.explanation: Only (i) and (iii) are correct: both classes have a tympanum for the ear, and crocodiles have a four-chambered heart while frogs have a three-chambered heart. Reptiles have internal fertilisation and direct development, so (ii) and (iv) are wrong. Ichthyophis is a limbless amphibian, not a reptile.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following animals have an open circulatory system?
Prawn, Balanoglossus, Nereis, Petromyzon, Scorpion
questions.explanation: Arthropods (prawn, scorpion) and hemichordates (Balanoglossus) have an open circulatory system. Annelids such as Nereis and chordates such as Petromyzon have closed circulation.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A marine animal has the following features: it is triploblastic and coelomate, its body is unsegmented, its digestive tract is complete, it has no excretory system, and its larva is bilaterally symmetrical while the adult is radially symmetrical. This animal is most likely:
questions.explanation: The lack of an excretory system and a radial adult with a bilateral larva are features of echinoderms, and Ophiura (brittle star) is an echinoderm. Balanoglossus has a proboscis gland for excretion, while Chaetopleura and Loligo are bilateral molluscs whose gills also perform excretion.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following is oviparous?
questions.explanation: The platypus is an egg-laying (oviparous) mammal. Bats, elephants and whales are viviparous.
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 4 (MCQ Q9)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which option correctly contrasts Porifera with Coelenterata?
options: Porifera: digestion only intracellular; Coelenterata: digestion both extracellular and intracellular
Porifera: radial symmetry; Coelenterata: mostly asymmetrical
Porifera: tissue level of organisation; Coelenterata: cellular level of organisation
Porifera: mouth on hypostome; Coelenterata: water exits through osculum
questions.explanation: Sponges digest food only within cells, whereas cnidarians digest both in the gastro-vascular cavity and within cells. The other options swap the features of the two phyla.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In Cephalochordata, the notochord extends from head to tail and persists throughout life.
Statement II: In Vertebrata, the notochord is present only in the larval tail.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation: Statement I correctly describes cephalochordates such as Branchiostoma. A notochord restricted to the larval tail is a feature of Urochordata. In vertebrates, the notochord is present in the embryo and is replaced by a vertebral column in the adult.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about ctenophores are correct?
(i) They are exclusively marine.
(ii) They are radially symmetrical.
(iii) They are diploblastic.
(iv) They reproduce both asexually and sexually.
(v) Fertilisation is internal.
(vi) Bioluminescence is well-marked.
(vii) Sexes are not separate.
questions.explanation: Statements (i), (ii), (iii), (vi) and (vii) are correct, giving five in total. Ctenophores reproduce only by sexual means, and their fertilisation is external, so (iv) and (v) are wrong.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following features correctly describes members of class Cyclostomata such as Petromyzon?
options: Body covered with minute placoid scales
questions.explanation: Cyclostomes are jawless vertebrates with a sucking, circular mouth. They have no scales and no paired fins, and their cranium and vertebral column are cartilaginous.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Apis
(b) Bombyx
(c) Laccifer
(d) Locusta
List-II
(i) Gregarious pest
(ii) Lac insect
(iii) Honey bee
(iv) Silkworm
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: Apis is the honey bee, Bombyx is the silkworm, Laccifer is the lac insect and Locusta is the gregarious pest. The common trap is swapping Apis and Bombyx.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about phylum Arthropoda is incorrect?
options: The body is covered by a chitinous exoskeleton
More than two-thirds of all named species on earth are arthropods
Blood flows only within a closed network of arteries, veins and capillaries
Members are mostly oviparous and fertilisation is usually internal
questions.explanation: Arthropods have an open circulatory system, in which blood pumped out of the heart bathes the tissues directly. A closed circulatory system is a feature of annelids, so statement 3 is the incorrect one.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following is a non-poisonous snake?
questions.explanation: The python kills prey by constriction and is non-venomous. Cobra, viper and krait are poisonous snakes.
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 4 (MCQ Q10)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Read the following statements comparing chordates and non-chordates.
Statement I: In chordates the heart is ventral, whereas in non-chordates the heart, if present, is dorsal.
Statement II: In non-chordates the central nervous system is dorsal, solid and single.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation: Chordates have a ventral heart, and non-chordates have a dorsal heart when one is present, so Statement I is correct. In non-chordates the CNS is ventral, solid and double. A dorsal, hollow, single CNS is the chordate condition, so Statement II is incorrect.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): All vertebrates are chordates, but all chordates are not vertebrates.
Reason (R): Urochordates and cephalochordates possess a notochord but never develop a vertebral column.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Every vertebrate has a notochord in the embryo, so all vertebrates are chordates. The protochordates have a notochord but no vertebral column, which is exactly why some chordates are not vertebrates. R therefore correctly explains A.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Read the following statements about Aschelminthes.
Statement I: In roundworms, the body cavity is completely lined by mesoderm.
Statement II: Roundworms are dioecious, and females are often longer than males.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Roundworms are pseudocoelomates. Their mesoderm lies as scattered pouches between the ectoderm and endoderm rather than lining the cavity, so Statement I is wrong. They have separate sexes, and females are often longer than males, so Statement II is right.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Read the following statements.
Statement I: Hemichordates possess a true notochord in the collar region and are therefore now placed as a subphylum of Chordata.
Statement II: In Urochordata, the notochord is present only in the larval tail.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation: Hemichordates have only a stomochord, a rudimentary structure similar to a notochord, and are now placed as a separate phylum under non-chordata. Statement II is correct as written.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which of the following animals are cells performing the same function arranged into tissues, but tissues are not grouped into organs?
questions.explanation: Adamsia (sea anemone) is a coelenterate, so it shows the tissue level of organisation. Sycon is at the cellular level, Fasciola at the organ level and Pheretima at the organ-system level.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Ichthyophis is best described as:
questions.explanation: Ichthyophis is the limbless amphibian among the NCERT examples of Amphibia. Its lack of limbs can mislead students into calling it a snake or a fish.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
A. Physalia
B. Adamsia
C. Pennatula
D. Gorgonia
List-II
I. Sea-fan
II. Portuguese man-of-war
III. Sea-pen
IV. Sea anemone
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: The correct pairs are Physalia (Portuguese man-of-war), Adamsia (sea anemone), Pennatula (sea-pen) and Gorgonia (sea-fan). Students often confuse sea-pen with sea-fan, so learn the two genus names as a pair.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Anopheles, Culex and Aedes are arthropods that are best described as:
options: Insects of economic importance producing useful products
questions.explanation: These three mosquito genera are listed as vectors because they transmit disease-causing organisms. Locusta is the gregarious pest, and Limulus is the living fossil.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following correctly contrasts Platyhelminthes with Aschelminthes as described in NCERT?
options: Platyhelminthes have an excretory pore, whereas Aschelminthes excrete through flame cells
Platyhelminthes have an incomplete digestive system and are hermaphrodite, whereas Aschelminthes have a complete alimentary canal and are dioecious
Both phyla possess an open circulatory system but lack respiratory organs
Platyhelminthes are pseudocoelomate, whereas Aschelminthes are acoelomate
questions.explanation: Flatworms have a single gut opening and the sexes are not separate, while roundworms have a complete gut with a muscular pharynx and separate sexes. The other options swap the excretory structures and body-cavity types, or wrongly give these worms a circulatory system, which is absent in both.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Hemichordata is now placed as a separate phylum under non-chordata.
Reason (R): Hemichordates have a rudimentary structure called stomochord in the collar region, which is similar to the notochord.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements agree with NCERT. However, the notochord-like stomochord is the reason hemichordates were once kept under Chordata, so it cannot explain why they are now placed among non-chordates.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following molluscs is correctly matched with its common name?
questions.explanation: Pinctada is the pearl oyster. Sepia is the cuttlefish, Loligo is the squid, Dentalium is the tusk shell, Chaetopleura is the chiton, Aplysia is the sea-hare and Octopus is the devil fish.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Sponges are said to show a cellular level of organisation because:
options: Their cells performing the same function are grouped into tissues
Their cells are arranged as loose cell aggregates
Their tissues are grouped to form organs
Their organs are associated to form organ systems
questions.explanation: In sponges the cells form only loose aggregates, with some division of labour, and they are not organised into true tissues. Tissue level organisation begins with coelenterates.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is a freshwater sponge?
questions.explanation: NCERT gives Spongilla as the freshwater sponge. Euspongia is the bath sponge, and Scypha is another name for Sycon, which is marine.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: External ears, or pinnae, are a characteristic feature of which of the following classes?
questions.explanation: Pinnae are present in mammals. In amphibians and reptiles, a tympanum represents the ear, and reptiles have no external ear openings.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A student examines a transverse section of a worm. The section is circular in outline. A body cavity lies between the body wall and the gut, but mesoderm does not line this cavity and is seen only as scattered patches. A muscular pharynx is visible in a section taken near the anterior end, and male and female individuals are found separately. The worm is most likely:
questions.explanation: A circular cross-section, a pseudocoelom, a muscular pharynx and separate sexes are all features of roundworms such as the hookworm Ancylostoma. Fasciola and Planaria are flat acoelomates, and Nereis has a true coelom lined by mesoderm.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following animals are oviparous and show direct development?
Calotes, Columba, Rana, Pila, Catla, Ornithorhynchus, Hyla
questions.explanation: Calotes (reptile), Columba (bird), Catla (bony fish) and Ornithorhynchus (egg-laying mammal) are oviparous with direct development. Rana and Hyla are amphibians, and Pila is a mollusc; all three have indirect development, so the count is 4.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following coelenterates is commonly called the brain coral?
questions.explanation: Meandrina is the brain coral. Pennatula is the sea-pen, Gorgonia is the sea-fan and Physalia is the Portuguese man-of-war.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (level of organisation) with List-II (animal):
List-I
A. Cellular level
B. Tissue level
C. Organ level
D. Organ-system level
List-II
I. Taenia
II. Pila
III. Spongilla
IV. Pleurobrachia
questions.explanation: Spongilla (sponge) is at the cellular level and Pleurobrachia (ctenophore) at the tissue level. Taenia (flatworm) is at the organ level and Pila (mollusc) at the organ-system level. Ctenophores, like cnidarians, have not reached the organ level.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about phylum Mollusca is incorrect?
options: The body is unsegmented, with a distinct head, a muscular foot and a visceral hump
The feather-like gills in the mantle cavity have both respiratory and excretory functions
The mantle cavity is the space between the calcareous shell and the mantle
The anterior head region bears sensory tentacles
questions.explanation: The mantle cavity is the space between the visceral hump and the mantle, not between the shell and the mantle. The other three statements match NCERT.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Laccifer
(b) Locusta
(c) Aedes
(d) Bombyx
List-II
(i) Gregarious pest
(ii) Disease vector
(iii) Lac insect
(iv) Silkworm
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: Laccifer is the lac insect and Locusta is a gregarious pest. Aedes is a mosquito vector, and Bombyx is the silkworm. A common trap is swapping Laccifer and Bombyx, since both are economically useful insects.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about phylum Echinodermata are correct?
(i) The endoskeleton is made of calcareous ossicles.
(ii) The larvae are radially symmetrical, while the adults are bilaterally symmetrical.
(iii) The mouth is on the ventral side and the anus on the dorsal side.
(iv) A proboscis gland serves as the excretory organ.
(v) Fertilisation is usually external, and development is indirect with a free-swimming larva.
questions.explanation: Statements (i), (iii) and (v) are correct. The symmetry in (ii) is reversed: adults are radial and larvae are bilateral. Echinoderms have no excretory system, and the proboscis gland belongs to hemichordates.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following serve as respiratory organs in arthropods?
Gills, book gills, book lungs, tracheal system, nephridia, malpighian tubules
questions.explanation: Arthropods respire through gills, book gills, book lungs or a tracheal system, which makes four. Nephridia are annelid excretory organs, and malpighian tubules are excretory organs in arthropods.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In members of phylum Mollusca, the radula is best described as:
options: A feather-like gill lying in the mantle cavity
A file-like rasping organ in the mouth used for feeding
A soft, spongy fold of skin covering the visceral hump
A sensory tentacle on the anterior head region
questions.explanation: The radula is a file-like rasping organ in the mouth that molluscs use for feeding. The other options describe the gills, the mantle and the head tentacles.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following groups are coelomates?
Annelids, Molluscs, Aschelminthes, Hemichordates, Platyhelminthes, Echinoderms, Arthropods, Ctenophores
questions.explanation: The coelomates in the list are annelids, molluscs, hemichordates, echinoderms and arthropods, which makes five. Aschelminthes are pseudocoelomates, platyhelminthes are acoelomates, and ctenophores are diploblastic with no coelom.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements comparing Coelenterata and Ctenophora is INCORRECT?
options: Members of both phyla are diploblastic, show tissue level of organisation and lack a coelom
Some cnidarians, such as corals, have a skeleton composed of calcium carbonate
Ctenophores reproduce by both asexual and sexual means and show internal fertilisation
Ctenophores are exclusively marine, and bioluminescence is well-marked in them
questions.explanation: Ctenophores reproduce only sexually, with external fertilisation and indirect development, so option 3 is incorrect. Asexual reproduction does occur in cnidarians, for example when polyps produce medusae, and this is the likely source of confusion.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which of the following phyla is the blood circulated through a series of vessels such as arteries, veins and capillaries?
questions.explanation: Annelids have a closed circulatory system, so blood flows only within vessels. Arthropods and hemichordates have an open type, and sponges have no circulatory system at all.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Cartilaginous fishes such as Scoliodon have to swim constantly.
Reason (R): Chondrichthyes lack an air bladder.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Chondrichthyes have no air bladder to regulate buoyancy, so they must keep swimming to avoid sinking. R therefore directly explains A.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(A) Salpa
(B) Myxine
(C) Scoliodon
(D) Ichthyophis
List-II
(i) Tetrapoda
(ii) Agnatha
(iii) Urochordata
(iv) Pisces
Choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation: Salpa is a urochordate. Myxine (hagfish) is a jawless cyclostome, so it belongs to Agnatha. Scoliodon is a cartilaginous fish under Pisces. Ichthyophis is a limbless amphibian, but amphibians are still classed under Tetrapoda.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In Balanoglossus, the excretory organ is the:
questions.explanation: Hemichordates excrete through the proboscis gland. Flame cells belong to flatworms, nephridia to annelids, and Malpighian tubules to arthropods.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A diagrammatic cross-section of an animal shows an outer ectoderm and an inner endoderm lining the gut. Between them is a body cavity, and mesoderm is present only as scattered pouches; it does not line the cavity. Which animal shows this body plan?
questions.explanation: A body cavity not lined by mesoderm, with mesoderm in scattered pouches, is a pseudocoelom, as seen in aschelminthes such as Ascaris. Fasciola is acoelomate, Pheretima is a true coelomate and Adamsia is diploblastic.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Two vertebrate specimens are described.
Specimen X: jawless, circular sucking mouth, body without scales and paired fins, lives as an ectoparasite on fishes.
Specimen Y: powerful jaws, ventral mouth, separate gill slits without operculum, claspers on pelvic fins of males, and a poison sting.
Identify X and Y.
questions.explanation: X fits a cyclostome such as Petromyzon (lamprey). Y is a cartilaginous fish with a poison sting, which is Trygon (sting ray). Torpedo has electric organs rather than a sting, and Scoliodon has jaws, so it cannot be X.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Members of Chondrichthyes have to swim constantly to avoid sinking.
Reason (R): Chondrichthyes lack an air bladder.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Cartilaginous fishes have no air bladder to regulate buoyancy. They must therefore keep swimming so they do not sink, so R directly explains A.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following pairs of animals has non glandular skin
questions.explanation: Reptiles such as chameleons and turtles have dry, cornified skin without glands. Frogs have moist glandular skin, and mammals like tigers have sweat and oil glands.
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 4 (MCQ Q4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (genus) with List-II (common name).
List-I:
(a) Hyla
(b) Calotes
(c) Hemidactylus
(d) Bangarus
List-II:
(i) Wall lizard
(ii) Krait
(iii) Tree frog
(iv) Garden lizard
questions.explanation: Hyla is the tree frog, Calotes the garden lizard, Hemidactylus the wall lizard and Bangarus the krait. Do not confuse Calotes (garden lizard) with Hemidactylus (wall lizard) or with Chameleon (tree lizard).
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In hemichordates such as Balanoglossus, the circulatory system is of the open type.
Reason (R): Hemichordates are triploblastic and coelomate animals.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true according to NCERT. However, having a coelom does not explain why circulation is open. Annelids and chordates are also coelomates, yet they have a closed circulatory system.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In members of phylum Arthropoda, excretion takes place mainly through:
questions.explanation: Arthropods excrete through malpighian tubules. Nephridia are the excretory organs of annelids, flame cells belong to flatworms, and the proboscis gland belongs to hemichordates.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: An animal shows the following features: dry cornified skin with epidermal scales, a tympanum but no external ear opening, a three-chambered heart, internal fertilisation and direct development. It is most likely:
questions.explanation: Dry cornified scaly skin, internal fertilisation and direct development point to a reptile, and the three-chambered heart excludes crocodiles, so Calotes (garden lizard) fits. Rana and Ichthyophis are amphibians with moist skin, external fertilisation and indirect development.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to the comparison of chordates and non-chordates, where is the heart located in chordates?
questions.explanation: Chordates have a ventral heart. In non-chordates the heart, when present, is dorsal. This reverses the position of the nerve cord, which is dorsal in chordates and ventral in non-chordates.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In echinoderms, the mouth lies on the lower (ventral) side and the anus on the upper (dorsal) side.
Reason (R): Adult echinoderms are bilaterally symmetrical, while their larvae are radially symmetrical.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are false
questions.explanation: The digestive system of echinoderms is complete, with a ventral mouth and a dorsal anus, so A is true. R reverses the facts: adults are radially symmetrical and larvae are bilaterally symmetrical.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(a) Arthropods have an open circulatory system.
(b) Hemichordates have a closed circulatory system.
(c) Circulation in cyclostomes is of the closed type.
(d) Annelids possess a closed circulatory system.
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Arthropods have open circulation, while cyclostomes and annelids have closed circulation. Hemichordates, despite being close to chordates, have an open circulatory system, so statement (b) is false.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Bioluminescence, the property of a living organism to emit light, is described as well-marked in which of the following animals?
questions.explanation: Pleurobrachia is a ctenophore (comb jelly), and bioluminescence is a well-marked feature of ctenophores. Adamsia and Meandrina are cnidarians, and Spongilla is a sponge.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
1. The digestive tract of birds has additional chambers, the crop and the gizzard.
2. In birds, air sacs connected to the lungs supplement respiration.
3. All mammals are viviparous.
4. Both birds and mammals have a four-chambered heart and are homoiothermous.
5. The hind limbs of birds generally lack scales.
6. External ears (pinnae) are present in mammals.
7. Delphinus and Balaenoptera, being aquatic, respire through gills.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2, 4 and 6 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong because Ornithorhynchus (platypus) is oviparous. Statement 5 is wrong because the hind limbs of birds generally bear scales, and statement 7 is wrong because all mammals, including aquatic dolphins and whales, respire by lungs.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In sponges, digestion takes place inside cells.
Statement II: In sponges, eggs and sperms are produced by different individuals.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation: Digestion in sponges is intracellular, so Statement I is correct. Statement II is wrong because sponges are hermaphrodite, meaning the same individual produces both eggs and sperms.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: An animal has the following features: it lays eggs, maintains a constant body temperature, has hair on its skin, and feeds its young with milk from mammary glands. Which conclusion is correct?
options: It belongs to Aves, because egg-laying combined with homoiothermy is an avian feature
It belongs to Reptilia, because it is oviparous with direct development
It belongs to Mammalia and is like Ornithorhynchus, an oviparous exception among mammals
It belongs to Mammalia, and Macropus is another example of such an oviparous mammal
questions.explanation: Hair and mammary glands are diagnostic of mammals, so egg-laying does not exclude the animal from Mammalia. NCERT cites Ornithorhynchus (platypus) as the oviparous example. Macropus (kangaroo) is viviparous, so the last option is wrong.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Echinoderms are triploblastic even though their adults show radial symmetry, like coelenterates.
Reason (R): The larvae of echinoderms are bilaterally symmetrical.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
