questions.explanation: Both statements are true: echinoderms have three germ layers, and their larvae are bilateral while the adults are radial. However, larval symmetry does not explain why they are triploblastic; germ layers and symmetry are independent features.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Body cavity is the cavity present between body wall and gut wall. In some animals the body cavity is not lined by mesoderm. Such animals are called
questions.explanation: In pseudocoelomates, mesoderm occurs as scattered pouches between ectoderm and endoderm instead of lining the body cavity. Aschelminthes are an example.
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 4 (MCQ Q12)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following animals are hermaphrodite (sexes not separate)?
Sycon, Pleurobrachia, Taenia, Ascaris, Pheretima, Nereis, Hirudinaria
questions.explanation: Sycon, Pleurobrachia, Taenia, Pheretima (earthworm) and Hirudinaria (leech) are hermaphrodite, which makes five. Ascaris and Nereis are dioecious; the trap is assuming all annelids are monoecious.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In flatworms such as Fasciola, the specialised cells called flame cells are mainly concerned with:
options: Locomotion and attachment to the host
questions.explanation: NCERT states that flame cells help in osmoregulation and excretion in Platyhelminthes. Attachment to the host is the job of hooks and suckers, not flame cells.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: On the basis of its body cavity, the liver fluke Fasciola is best described as:
questions.explanation: Platyhelminthes such as Fasciola have no body cavity between the body wall and the gut, so they are acoelomates. Pseudocoelom is the condition seen in roundworms.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Hemichordates possess a stomochord, a structure similar to the notochord, in the collar region.
Statement II: Hemichordata is therefore placed as a sub-phylum under phylum Chordata.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Hemichordates do have a rudimentary stomochord in the collar region. However, Hemichordata, which was earlier treated as a chordate sub-phylum, is now placed as a separate phylum under non-chordates.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Ctenophora is incorrect?
options: They reproduce only by sexual means
Fertilisation is internal and development is direct
Their body bears eight external rows of ciliated comb plates
questions.explanation: Ctenophores have external fertilisation with indirect development, so this is the incorrect statement. The other three statements correctly describe comb jellies.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which of the following groups is the notochord present only in the larval tail?
questions.explanation: In urochordates (tunicates) such as Ascidia, the notochord is found only in the tail of the larva. In cephalochordates it runs from head to tail throughout life. Hemichordates have only a stomochord, not a true notochord.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Birds have a fully ossified endoskeleton, and their long bones are hollow with air cavities
In birds, air sacs replace the lungs as the main respiratory organs, whereas mammals respire by lungs
Mammals have different types of teeth in the jaw and possess external pinnae
Both birds and mammals have a four-chambered heart and can maintain a constant body temperature
questions.explanation: Birds respire by lungs. Their air sacs are connected to the lungs and only supplement respiration; they do not replace the lungs. All the other statements match NCERT.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(A) Asterias
(B) Echinus
(C) Antedon
(D) Cucumaria
List-II
(i) Sea lily
(ii) Sea cucumber
(iii) Star fish
(iv) Sea urchin
Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation: Asterias is the star fish, Echinus the sea urchin, Antedon the sea lily and Cucumaria the sea cucumber. A common trap is confusing Echinus (sea urchin) with Asterias (star fish).
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Pteropus is placed in class Mammalia even though it is adapted for flight.
Reason (R): Pteropus has hair on its skin and nourishes its young with milk from mammary glands.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Pteropus, the flying fox, is a viviparous mammal. It is classified as a mammal because it has hair and mammary glands, which are the defining mammalian features, not on the basis of flight. So R correctly explains A.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements comparing Annelida and Arthropoda is INCORRECT?
options: Both phyla are bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic, segmented and coelomate with organ-system level of organisation.
Respiration in arthropods may occur through gills, book gills, book lungs or a tracheal system.
In arthropods, excretion occurs through malpighian tubules and the blood remains confined within arteries, veins and capillaries.
Arthropods account for over two-thirds of all named species on earth, making Arthropoda the largest animal phylum.
questions.explanation: Malpighian tubules are correct for arthropods, but their circulatory system is open, with tissues bathed directly in blood. Blood confined within vessels describes the closed circulation of annelids, and this half-true mix is the trap.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Delphinus and Balaenoptera are placed in class Mammalia even though they live in water.
Statement II: Mammals have teeth of only one type in their jaws.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: The dolphin and the blue whale are aquatic mammals, so Statement I is correct. Mammals have different types of teeth in the jaw, so Statement II is incorrect.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match the column A with column B and choose the correct option
Column I: A. Porifera; B. Aschelminthes; C. Annelida; D. Arthropoda; E. Echinodermata
Column II: i. Canal system; ii. Water-vascular system; iii. Muscular pharynx; iv. Jointed appendages; v. Metameres
questions.explanation: Sponges have a canal system and roundworms a muscular pharynx. Annelids are metamerically segmented, arthropods have jointed appendages, and echinoderms have a water-vascular system.
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 4 (MCQ Q13)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) Taenia
(B) Fasciola
(C) Wuchereria
(D) Ancylostoma
List-II
(I) Filaria worm
(II) Hookworm
(III) Tapeworm
(IV) Liver fluke
Choose the correct answer.
questions.explanation: Taenia is the tapeworm and Fasciola is the liver fluke (both flatworms). Wuchereria is the filaria worm and Ancylostoma is the hookworm (both roundworms).
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Nereis is a dioecious annelid.
Reason (R): Earthworms and leeches are monoecious.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true: Nereis has separate sexes, while Pheretima and Hirudinaria are monoecious. However, the sexual condition of earthworms and leeches does not explain why Nereis is dioecious.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Read the following statements.
Statement I: In sponges, cells are arranged as loose aggregates, with some division of labour among them.
Statement II: In coelenterates, cells performing the same function are grouped into tissues.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation: Sponges show the cellular level of organisation, with loose cell aggregates and some division of labour. Coelenterates show the tissue level, where cells with the same function form tissues.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about sponges is correct?
options: Water enters through the osculum and leaves through the ostia
Choanocytes line only the osculum and are absent from the canals
The water transport system serves food gathering, respiratory exchange and waste removal, as sponges lack separate respiratory and circulatory systems
Food is digested extracellularly in the spongocoel by enzymes secreted from spongin fibres
questions.explanation: Sponges have no respiratory or circulatory systems (Table 4.2), so the canal system handles food gathering, gas exchange and waste removal. The other options reverse the water flow, misplace the choanocytes, or describe extracellular digestion when sponge digestion is intracellular.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Pisces and Tetrapoda are the two super classes of division Gnathostomata.
Statement II: Class Cyclostomata is placed under super class Pisces because its members bear paired fins.
Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation: Gnathostomata is divided into the super classes Pisces (with fins) and Tetrapoda (with limbs). Cyclostomes are jawless and lack paired fins, so they belong to Agnatha, not Pisces.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match the following list of animals with their level of organisation.
Division of Labour (Column I): A. Organ level; B. Cellular aggregate level; C. Tissue level; D. Organ system level
Animal (Column II): i. Pheretima; ii. Fasciola; iii. Spongilla; iv. Obelia
Choose the correct match showing division of labour with animal example.
questions.explanation: Sponges like Spongilla show the cellular aggregate level and cnidarians like Obelia the tissue level. Flatworms like Fasciola show the organ level, and annelids like Pheretima the organ system level.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about members of phylum Porifera are correct?
I. Water enters the body through the osculum, passes into the spongocoel and leaves through the ostia.
II. Choanocytes (collar cells) line the spongocoel and the canals.
III. Digestion takes place inside cells.
IV. Fertilisation is external and development is direct.
V. Eggs and sperms are produced by the same individual.
questions.explanation: Statements II, III and V are correct, because collar cells line the canal system, digestion is intracellular and sponges are hermaphrodite. Statement I reverses the water path, since water enters through the ostia and exits through the osculum. Statement IV is wrong because fertilisation is internal and development is indirect, with a distinct larval stage.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to NCERT, which of the following is the most unique characteristic of class Mammalia?
questions.explanation: Mammary glands, which nourish the young, are described as the most unique mammalian feature. A four-chambered heart, homoiothermy and internal fertilisation are also found in birds.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following groups are true coelomates?
Annelida, Aschelminthes, Mollusca, Platyhelminthes, Arthropoda, Ctenophora, Echinodermata, Hemichordata
questions.explanation: Annelida, Mollusca, Arthropoda, Echinodermata and Hemichordata are coelomates, giving a total of five. Aschelminthes are pseudocoelomates, Platyhelminthes are acoelomates, and ctenophores are diploblastic with no coelom.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following features are shared by both Taenia and Ascaris?
(i) Bilateral symmetry
(ii) Triploblastic body
(iii) Internal fertilisation
(iv) Separate sexes
(v) Complete alimentary canal
(vi) Flame cells for excretion
questions.explanation: Both phyla are bilaterally symmetrical and triploblastic, and both show internal fertilisation, giving three shared features. Separate sexes and a complete gut occur only in Ascaris, while flame cells occur only in flatworms.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the aquatic annelid Nereis, the lateral appendages called parapodia mainly help in:
questions.explanation: Nereis has lateral appendages, the parapodia, which help it swim. Excretion and osmoregulation in annelids are carried out by nephridia, not parapodia.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (genus) with List-II (common name):
List-I
(a) Pinctada
(b) Sepia
(c) Dentalium
(d) Chaetopleura
List-II
(i) Tusk shell
(ii) Chiton
(iii) Pearl oyster
(iv) Cuttlefish
questions.explanation: Pinctada is the pearl oyster, Sepia the cuttlefish, Dentalium the tusk shell and Chaetopleura the chiton. A common trap is swapping tusk shell and chiton.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (genus) with List-II (common name).
List-I
(A) Pristis
(B) Exocoetus
(C) Pteropus
(D) Antedon
List-II
(i) Flying fox
(ii) Sea lily
(iii) Saw fish
(iv) Flying fish
questions.explanation: Pristis is the saw fish, Exocoetus is the flying fish, Pteropus is the flying fox (a mammal) and Antedon is the sea lily (an echinoderm). Do not confuse the flying fish (a bony fish) with the flying fox (a mammal).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A marine, worm-like animal shows these features: bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic and coelomate, open circulatory system, respiration through gills, separate sexes, external fertilisation and indirect development. Which structure would this animal most likely possess?
options: A water vascular system used for locomotion and food capture
A proboscis gland functioning as the excretory organ
A notochord extending from head to tail and persisting throughout life
questions.explanation: These features fit a hemichordate such as Balanoglossus, whose excretory organ is the proboscis gland. A water vascular system belongs to echinoderms, which are radially symmetrical as adults. Molluscs with a radula are not worm-like and have internal shells or feet. Cephalochordates have a persistent notochord but a closed circulatory system.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: In Salpa, the notochord is restricted to the larval tail
In vertebrates, the embryonic notochord is replaced by a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column in the adult
Cephalochordates are mostly freshwater animals in which the notochord is confined to the head region
Division Gnathostomata includes both Pisces and Tetrapoda
questions.explanation: Protochordates, including cephalochordates, are exclusively marine. Their notochord extends from head to tail and lasts throughout life, so it is not confined to the head. The other three statements agree with NCERT.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Hydra and Adamsia represent the polyp form, which is sessile and cylindrical.
Statement II: Aurelia (jelly fish) represents a sessile, cylindrical polyp that lacks a free-swimming stage.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Hydra and Adamsia are sessile, cylindrical polyps, so Statement I is correct. Aurelia is an umbrella-shaped, free-swimming medusa, so Statement II is incorrect.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Lateral appendages called parapodia, which help in swimming, are found in which of the following annelids?
questions.explanation: Parapodia are lateral swimming appendages of aquatic annelids such as Nereis. Pheretima (earthworm) and Hirudinaria (leech) lack them, and Limulus is an arthropod, not an annelid.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following features are characteristic of non-chordates?
(a) Central nervous system ventral, solid and double
(b) Heart dorsal (if present)
(c) Gill slits absent
(d) Post-anal tail present
(e) Notochord absent
(f) Central nervous system dorsal, hollow and single
questions.explanation: Features (a), (b), (c) and (e) belong to non-chordates. A post-anal tail (d) and a dorsal, hollow, single nerve cord (f) are chordate features.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following features are correctly attributed to phylum Annelida?
(i) Closed circulatory system
(ii) Nephridia for osmoregulation and excretion
(iii) Paired ganglia connected by lateral nerves to a double ventral nerve cord
(iv) Body covered by a chitinous exoskeleton
(v) Excretion through malpighian tubules
questions.explanation: Annelids have a closed circulation, nephridia, and paired ganglia joined to a double ventral nerve cord, so statements (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct. The chitinous exoskeleton and malpighian tubules are arthropod features, so (iv) and (v) are wrong.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Ascaris is described as a pseudocoelomate animal.
Reason (R): In Ascaris, the body cavity is not lined by mesoderm; instead, mesoderm is present as scattered pouches between the ectoderm and the endoderm.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: A pseudocoelom is defined as a body cavity that is not lined by mesoderm, with mesoderm present only as scattered pouches. That definition is exactly why Ascaris is a pseudocoelomate, so R correctly explains A.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) All vertebrates are chordates, but all chordates are not vertebrates.
(ii) Division Agnatha is represented by class Cyclostomata, whose members lack jaws.
(iii) Pisces and Tetrapoda are super classes placed under division Gnathostomata.
(iv) In Urochordata, the notochord persists throughout life in the tail region.
(v) Vertebrates have a ventral muscular heart with two, three or four chambers and paired appendages in the form of fins or limbs.
(vi) Hemichordata is currently treated as a subphylum of Chordata because it has a stomochord.
questions.explanation: Statements (i), (ii), (iii) and (v) are correct. Statement (iv) is wrong because the urochordate notochord occurs only in the larval tail. Statement (vi) is wrong because Hemichordata is now a separate non-chordate phylum; its stomochord is only similar to a notochord.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A non-chordate animal has the following features: organ-system level of organisation, a complete digestive system, and blood that never leaves vessels to bathe tissues directly. Which of the following fits this description?
questions.explanation: Nereis is an annelid, so it has organ-system organisation, a complete gut and a closed circulatory system. Prawn (arthropod) and Balanoglossus (hemichordate) have open circulation. Ascaris has no circulatory system.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which member of Platyhelminthes is noted in NCERT for its high capacity for regeneration?
questions.explanation: NCERT names Planaria as a flatworm with high regeneration capacity. Ancylostoma is a roundworm, not a flatworm.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a sponge, which sequence correctly traces the path of water through the canal system?
questions.explanation: Water enters through the minute pores (ostia) in the body wall, reaches the central cavity (spongocoel), and leaves through the osculum. A common trap is to reverse the roles of the ostia and the osculum.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Birds and mammals share one of the following characteristics as a common feature.
questions.explanation: Both birds and mammals are homoiothermous (warm blooded), keeping a constant body temperature. Pneumatic bones are found only in birds, and viviparity is mostly a mammalian feature.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The spongocoel and the canals of a sponge are lined by:
questions.explanation: Choanocytes, also called flagellated collar cells, line the spongocoel and the canals. Cnidoblasts and nematocysts belong to coelenterates, and flame cells belong to flatworms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The notochord is best described as a:
options: Ectodermally derived hollow tube on the dorsal side
Mesodermally derived rod-like structure on the dorsal side
Endodermally derived rod on the ventral side
Mesodermally derived solid cord on the ventral side
questions.explanation: The notochord is a rod-like structure that arises from mesoderm on the dorsal side during embryonic development. The dorsal hollow tube is the nerve cord, which is a different structure.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental characteristic of phylum Chordata?
questions.explanation: A ventral, solid and double nerve cord is a non-chordate feature. Chordates are defined by a notochord, a dorsal hollow single nerve cord and paired pharyngeal gill slits.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The digestive system of Platyhelminthes is described as incomplete because:
options: Digestion in it is entirely intracellular
It has a single opening that serves as both mouth and anus
It has a mouth but the anus opens into a cloaca
questions.explanation: A digestive system is incomplete when only one opening to the outside works as both mouth and anus. A complete system has two separate openings, a mouth and an anus.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Both Hydra and Fasciola have a digestive system with a single opening to the outside.
Statement II: Fasciola, like Hydra, exhibits only the tissue level of organisation.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation: Both animals have an incomplete gut. Hydra has a gastro-vascular cavity with only a mouth, and the flatworm gut also has a single opening. However, Fasciola (a platyhelminth) shows the organ level of organisation, not the tissue level, so a shared gut type does not mean a shared level of organisation.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In the subphylum Vertebrata, the embryonic notochord is replaced by a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column in the adult.
Statement II: In Chondrichthyes, the notochord is persistent throughout life.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation: NCERT states both facts: vertebrates replace the notochord with a vertebral column, and Chondrichthyes retain a persistent notochord throughout life. Students often wrongly assume that persistence applies only to Cephalochordata.
